- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.7), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days), especially if sentiment was neutral or positive prior — apply lagged correction by 1-2 days.
- Forecast errors cluster near the end of the 30-day horizon — particularly days 25–30 — suggest model overreacts to recent sentiment or data; dampen tail end of forecast.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; introduce a “sentiment pivot” rule: if sentiment drops below 0.3 after day 10, reduce forecast slope by 10–15%.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.7) — especially if recent sentiment is trending downward — apply a “sentiment-weighted mean” correction: average of recent 5-day sentiment × 0.5 + recent price trend × 0.5.
